annotations.note: When the term <val>messageId</val> is used in these documents, it *doesn't* refer to the Message-ID email header. It is an internal tracking number that does not remain after a restart. Nor does it follow an email that has been moved to a different folder.

annotations.warning: Some functions in this API potentially return a lot of messages. See $(doc:guides/messageLists) for more information.

description: The messages API allows to access and manage the user's messages.

events.description: Fired when one or more properties of a message have been updated.
events.name: onUpdated

events.description: Fired when messages have been moved.
events.name: onMoved

events.description: Fired when messages have been copied.
events.name: onCopied

events.description: Fired when messages have been permanently deleted.
events.name: onDeleted

events.description: Fired when a new message is received, and has been handled by message filters and junk classification. Filters running after junk classification may move the message again.

extraParameters.description: Monitor all folders (including all special use folders as defined by $(ref:folders.MailFolderSpecialUse)) instead of just inbox folders and normal folders.
extraParameters.name: monitorAllFolders

events.name: onNewMailReceived

functions.description: Gets all messages in a folder.
functions.name: list

sortOrder.description: The sort order for the returned messages. Ignored if <var>sortType</var> is not specified.

sortType.description: Specifies how the returned messages should be sorted. Default sort order is <var>descending</var>, if not specified otherwise. Returning sorted messages is faster than manually sorting the messages afterwards, but slower than returning the messages in their original order.

functions.description: Returns the next chunk of messages in a list. See $(doc:guides/messageLists) for more information.
functions.name: continueList

functions.description: Finalizes the specified list and terminates any process currently still adding messages.
functions.name: abortList

functions.description: Returns the specified message.
functions.name: get

functions.description: Returns the specified message, including all headers and MIME parts. Throws if the message could not be read, for example due to network issues.
functions.name: getFull

decodeContent.description: Whether to decode quoted-printable or base64 encoded content of message parts. Defaults to <var>true</var>.

decodeHeaders.description: Whether to decode RFC 2047 encoded headers of message parts. Defaults to <var>true</var>.

decrypt.description: Whether the message should be decrypted. If the message could not be decrypted, its parts are omitted. Defaults to <var>true</var>.

annotations.note: Unlike $(ref:messages.getFull), this function is not MIME-aware and simply returns every header line found before the first blank line that separates the headers from the RFC 822 message body. This includes headers such as <var>Content-Type</var> and <var>Content-Transfer-Encoding</var>, which are otherwise associated with a specific MIME part.

functions.description: Returns all message headers of the specified message, without MIME structure parsing. Throws an error if the message cannot be read, for example due to network issues. This function is significantly faster than $(ref:messages.getFull) when only the header information is required.
functions.name: getHeaders

decodeHeaders.description: Whether to decode RFC 2047 encoded headers. Defaults to <var>true</var>.

functions.description: Returns the raw content of a message. Throws if the message could not be read, for example due to network issues.
functions.name: getRaw

parameters.description: Either a $(ref:messages.MessageId) of an existing message, or a $(ref:messages.MessagePart) with raw header and raw content data representing a full RFC 822 message (the provided data will be used as-is without applying any further encoding). See the <var>decodeHeaders</var> and <var>decodeContent</var> options of $(ref:messages.getFull) for further details on how to retrieve a $(ref:messages.MessagePart) with raw values. You can use $(ref:messengerUtilities.decodeMimeHeader) and $(ref:messengerUtilities.encodeMimeHeader) to manipulate a raw MessagePart.
parameters.name: message

annotations.text: Working with binary strings is error prone and needs special handling:

code: * Decodes a binary string using the given encoding format and returns a
* JavaScript string. Produces mangled output if used with anything but a binary

data_format.description: The message can either be returned as a DOM File (default) or as a binary string. It is recommended to use the File format, because the DOM File object can be used as-is with the downloads API and has useful methods to access the content, like File.text() and File.arrayBuffer().

decrypt.description: Whether the message should be decrypted. Throws, if the message could not be decrypted.

functions.description: Lists the attachments of a message. If the message is encrypted, the attachments of the decrypted message are listed.
functions.name: listAttachments

annotations.note: A message usually contains only one inline text part per subtype, but technically messages can contain multiple inline text parts per subtype.

functions.description: Lists all inline text parts of a message. These parts are not returned by $(ref:messages.listAttachments) and usually make up the readable content of the message, mostly with content type <var>text/plain</var> or <var>text/html</var>. If a message only includes a part with content type <var>text/html</var>, the method $(ref:messengerUtilities.convertToPlainText) can be used to retreive a plain text version. If the message is encrypted, the inline text parts of the decrypted message are listed.
functions.name: listInlineTextParts

annotations.text: The most simple way to get the content of an attachment is to use the text() method of the returned File object:

functions.description: Gets the content of a $(ref:messages.MessageAttachment) as a File object. If the message is encrypted, the function retrieves the attachment from the decrypted message.
functions.name: getAttachmentFile

parameters.description: The <var>partName</var> of an attachment to be retrieved from the decrypted message.
parameters.name: partName

functions.description: Deletes the specified attachments and replaces them by placeholder text attachments with meta information about the original attachments and a text/x-moz-deleted content type. This permanently modifies the message. Deleting attachments of encrypted messages is not supported and will throw an ExtensionError.
functions.name: deleteAttachments

parameters.description: An array of attachments, identifying the to be deleted attachments by their <var>partName</var>.
parameters.name: partNames

functions.description: Opens the specified attachment.
functions.name: openAttachment

parameters.description: The ID of the tab associated with the message opening.
parameters.name: tabId

functions.description: Gets all messages that have the specified properties, or all messages if no properties are specified. Messages of unified mailbox folders are not included by default (as that could double the amount of returned messages), but explicitly specifying a unified mailbox folder is supported.
functions.name: query

accountId.description: Limits the search to the specified account(s). Accounts are searched in the specified order.

attachment.description: Whether the message has attachments, or not. Supports to specify a $(ref:messages.QueryRange) (min/max) instead of a simple boolean value (none/some).

author.description: Returns only messages with this value matching the author. The search value is a single email address, a name or a combination (e.g.: <var>Name <user@domain.org></var>). The address part of the search value (if provided) must match the author's address completely. The name part of the search value (if provided) must match the author's name partially. All matches are done case-insensitive.

autoPaginationTimeout.description: Set the timeout in ms after which results should be returned, even if the nominal number of messages-per-page has not yet been reached. Defaults to <var>1000</var> ms. Setting it to <var>0</var> will disable auto-pagination.

body.description: Returns only messages with this value in the body of the mail.

flagged.description: Returns only flagged (or unflagged if false) messages.

folderId.description: Limits the search to the specified folder(s). Folders are searched in the specified order. The <permission>accountsRead</permission> permission is required.

fromDate.description: Returns only messages with a date after this value.

fromMe.description: Returns only messages with the author's address matching any configured identity.

fullText.description: Returns only messages with this value somewhere in the mail (subject, body or author).

headerMessageId.description: Returns only messages with a Message-ID header matching this value.

junk.description: Returns only messages whith the specified junk state.

junkScore.description: Returns only messages with a junk score in the specified range.

messagesPerPage.description: Set the nominal number of messages-per-page for this query. Defaults to <var>100</var> messages.

new.description: Returns only messages with the specified new state.

online.description: Query the server directly instead of the local message database. Online queries currently only support querying the <var>headerMessageId</var> property. Currently only supported for NNTP accounts.

read.description: Returns only messages with the specified read state.

recipients.description: Returns only messages whose recipients match all specified addresses. The search value is a semicolon separated list of email addresses, names or combinations (e.g.: <var>Name <user@domain.org></var>). For a match, all specified addresses must equal a recipient's address completely and all specified names must match a recipient's name partially. All matches are done case-insensitive.

returnMessageListId.description: The messageListId is usually returned together with the first page, after some messages have been found. Enabling this option will change the return value of this function and return the messageListId directly.

size.description: Returns only messages with a size in the specified byte range.

subject.description: Returns only messages whose subject contains the provided string.

tags.description: Returns only messages with the specified tags. For a list of available tags, call the $(ref:messages.tags.list) method.

toDate.description: Returns only messages with a date before this value.

toMe.description: Returns only messages with at least one recipient address matching any configured identity.

functions.description: Updates message properties and tags. Updating external messages will throw an ExtensionError.
functions.name: update

functions.description: Moves messages to a specified folder. If the messages cannot be removed from the source folder, they will be copied instead of moved. Moving external messages will throw an ExtensionError.
functions.name: move

parameters.description: The IDs of the messages to move.
parameters.name: messageIds

parameters.description: The folder to move the messages to.
parameters.name: folderId

isUserAction.description: Whether this move operation should be treated as a user action, for example allowing undo.

functions.description: Copies messages to a specified folder.
functions.name: copy

parameters.description: The IDs of the messages to copy.
parameters.name: messageIds

parameters.description: The folder to copy the messages to.
parameters.name: folderId

isUserAction.description: Whether this copy operation should be treated as a user action, for example allowing undo.

functions.description: Deletes messages permanently, or moves them to the trash folder (honoring the account's deletion behavior settings). Deleting external messages will throw an ExtensionError. The deletePermanently parameter allows immediate permanent deletion, bypassing the trash folder.
functions.name: delete

parameters.description: The IDs of the messages to delete.
parameters.name: messageIds

choices.deprecated: Specify the options object instead of a plain boolean to delete messages permanently.
choices.description: Whether the message will be deleted permanently, regardless of the account's deletion behavior settings.

deletePermanently.description: Whether the message will be deleted permanently, regardless of the account's deletion behavior settings. A permanently deleted message cannot be restored, even if the action is defined as a user action. Use this with care!

isUserAction.description: Whether this copy operation should be treated as a user action, for example allowing undo.

functions.description: Imports a message into a folder. Supports local folders, POP and IMAP folders. Throws, if the destination folder already contains a message with the Message-ID of the message being imported.
functions.name: import

parameters.description: The folder to import the messages into.
parameters.name: folderId

functions.description:
Sends a message programmatically in the background without user interaction. If the send mode is not specified or set to <value>default</value>, the message will be sent directly if the user is online and placed in the user's outbox otherwise. The returned Promise fulfills once the message has been successfully sent or placed in the user's outbox. Throws when there has been an error while sending the message to the outgoing mail server.
**Note:** If no <value>deliveryFormat</value> is specified, the message is sent as plain text when the body contains no HTML formatting.
**Note:** It is possible to pass in a $(ref:compose.ComposeDetails) object as the <value>details</value> parameter, and it will be interpreted as a $(ref:messages.NewMessageDetails) object.
functions.name: sendMessage

headerMessageId.description: The header messageId of the outgoing message. Only included for actually sent messages.

messages.description: Copies of the sent message. The number of created copies depends on the applied file carbon copy configuration (fcc).

functions.description:
Saves a message programmatically as a draft or as a template in the background without user interaction. The save mode defaults to <value>draft</value>. The returned Promise fulfills once the message has been successfully saved. Throws when there has been an error while saving the message.
**Note:** If no <value>deliveryFormat</value> is specified, the message is saved as plain text when the body contains no HTML formatting.
functions.name: saveMessage

messages.description: The saved message(s). The number of saved messages depends on the applied file carbon copy configuration (fcc).

functions.description: Archives messages using the current settings. Archiving external messages will throw an ExtensionError.
functions.name: archive

parameters.description: The IDs of the messages to archive.
parameters.name: messageIds

types.description: A unique id representing a $(ref:messages.MessageHeader) and the associated message. This id doesn’t refer to the Message-ID email header. It is an internal tracking number that does not remain after a restart. Nor does it follow an email that has been moved to a different folder.

An inline part with content type <var>text/*</var>. These parts are not returned by $(ref:messages.listAttachments) and usually make up the readable content of the message, mostly with content type <var>text/plain</var> or <var>text/html</var>

content.description: The content of this inline text part.

contentType.description: The content type of the part. Most common types for inline text parts are <var>text/plain</var> and <var>text/html</var>. Possible other (deprecated) types are <var>text/richtext</var> and <var>text/enriched</var>. Some calendaring services include an inline text part with type <var>text/calendar</var>.

types.description: Content may either be a single email address, or a mailbox string (see RFC 5322, section 3.4). Use $(ref:messengerUtilities.parseMailboxString) to extract the name and/or the email from the mailbox string.

bccList.description: The Bcc recipients. Not populated for news/nntp messages.

ccList.description: The Cc recipients. Not populated for news/nntp messages.

date.description: The date and time when the message was sent, according to the Date header in the message.

external.description: Whether this message is a real message or an external message (opened from a file or from an attachment).

flagged.description: Whether this message is flagged (a.k.a. starred).

folder.description: The <permission>accountsRead</permission> permission is required for this property to be included. Not available for external or attached messages.

headerMessageId.description: The message-id header of the message.

headersOnly.description: Some account types (for example <var>pop3</var>) allow to download only the headers of the message, but not its body. The body of such messages will not be available.

junk.description: Whether the message has been marked as junk. Always <var>false</var> for news/nntp messages and external messages.

junkScore.description: The junk score associated with the message. Always <var>0</var> for news/nntp messages and external messages.

new.description: Whether the message has been received recently and is marked as new.

read.description: Whether the message has been marked as read. Not available for external or attached messages.

recipients.description: The To recipients. Not populated for news/nntp messages.

size.description: The total size of the message in bytes.

tags.description: Tags associated with this message. For a list of available tags, use $(ref:messages.tags.list).

id.description: Id of the message list, to be used with $(ref:messages.continueList) or $(ref:messages.abortList).

types.description: Represents an email message "part", which could be the whole message.

body.description: The quoted-printable or base64 decoded content of the part. Only present for parts with a content type of <var>text/*</var> and only if requested, see the <var>decodeContent</var> option of $(ref:messages.getFull). Use $(ref:messages.getAttachmentFile) to retrieve the content of parts which have a content type other than <var>text/*</var>.

decryptionStatus.description: The decryption status, only available for the root part.

headers.description: A dictionary object of RFC 2047 decoded part headers as key-value pairs, with the header name as key, and an array of headers as value. Only present if requested, see the decodeHeaders option of $(ref:messages.getFull).

name.description: Name of the part, if it is a file.

partName.description: The identifier of this part, used in $(ref:messages.getAttachmentFile).

rawBody.description: The raw content of the part. Only present if requested, see the <var>decodeContent</var> option of $(ref:messages.getFull).

rawHeaders.description: A dictionary object of raw part headers as key-value pairs, with the header name as key, and an array of headers as value. Only present if requested, see the decodeHeaders option of $(ref:messages.getFull).

size.description: The size of this part. The size of parts with content type message/rfc822 is not the actual message size (on disc), but the total size of its decoded body parts, excluding headers.

types.description: Message properties used in $(ref:messages.update) and $(ref:messages.import). They can also be monitored by $(ref:messages.onUpdated).

flagged.description: Whether the message is flagged (a.k.a starred).

junk.description: Whether the message is marked as junk. Only supported in $(ref:messages.update).

new.description: Whether the message is marked as new. Only supported in $(ref:messages.import).

read.description: Whether the message is marked as read.

tags.description: Tags associated with this message. For a list of available tags, call the $(ref:messages.tags.list) method.

types.description: The type of an attachment in a message.

annotations.text: The attachment's content is not part of the message but stored by a cloud provider.
The attachment's content was permanently removed and only a placeholder remains.
The attachment's content is stored in a detached local file.
The attachment's content is not part of the message but referenced by a link.

types.description: Represents an attachment in a message.

cloudFileUrl.description: The remote location a <var>cloudFile</var> attachment's content is stored at. Present for <var>cloudFile</var> attachments (see $(ref:messages.AttachmentType)), whose content is not part of the message.

contentDisposition.description: The content disposition of the attachment, for example <var>attachment</var> for normal attachments, or <var>inline</var> for inline attachments.

contentId.description: The content-id of this part. Available for related parts, which are referenced from other places inside the same message (e.g. inline images).

contentType.description: The content type of the attachment. A value of <var>text/x-moz-deleted</var> indicates that the original attachment was permanently deleted and replaced by a placeholder text attachment with some meta information about the original attachment.

headers.description: A dictionary object of RFC 2047 decoded attachment headers as key-value pairs, with the header name as key, and an array of headers as value.

linkUrl.description: The remote location the attachment's content is linked to. Present for <var>linked</var> attachments (see $(ref:messages.AttachmentType)), whose content is not part of the message and can be fetched from this url.

message.description: A MessageHeader, if this attachment is a message.

name.description: The name, as displayed to the user, of this attachment. This is usually but not always the filename of the attached file. For a <var>cloudFile</var> attachment, this is the real name of the linked file, when the message provides one.

partName.description: Identifies the MIME part of the message associated with this attachment.

size.description: The size in bytes of this attachment.

types.description: A dictionary object of headers as key-value pairs, with the header name as key, and an array of headers as value.

max.description: The maximum value required to match the query.

min.description: The minimum value required to match the query.

types.description: Details of a message to be sent.

additionalFccFolder.description: An additional fcc folder. Only effective for send operations ($(ref:messages.sendMessage)), has no effect for save operations ($(ref:messages.saveMessage)), which only ever store the message in the primary draft or template folder. For compatibility with $(ref:compose.ComposeDetails), setting an empty string is supported as well, but has no effect.

attachVCard.description: Wether or not the vCard of the used identity will be attached to the message during send.

attachments.description: Attachments to add to the message. **Note:** $(ref:compose.ComposeAttachments) are included as real file attachments, not as cloudFile links.

body.description: The HTML content for the message.

annotations.note: No <var>Content-Language</var> header is added if the user has enabled the <var>mail.suppress_content_language</var> preference.

contentLanguage.description: The languages of the message content, used for the Content-Language header. Each entry is a free-form language tag (for example en-US). If omitted, no Content-Language header is added. The i18n API's detectLanguage() can be used to derive a value from the message body, which should be converted to plain text first (for example via $(ref:messengerUtilities.convertToPlainText)), so that markup does not influence the detection.

deliveryFormat.description:
Defines the mime format of the sent message. Defaults to <value>auto</value>, which prefers to send plain text messages, if the specified body does not include any formatting.
**Note**: If a plain text body and an HTML body is included in the message, the plain text body is always derived from the included HTML body. It is not possible to specify two independent values via <value>body</value> and <value>plainTextBody</value>.

deliveryStatusNotification.description: Let the sender know when the recipient's server received the message. Not supported by all servers.

from.description: *Caution*: Setting a value for <val>from</val> does not change the used identity, it overrides the FROM header. Many email servers do not accept emails where the FROM header does not match the sender identity. Must be set to exactly one valid email address.

identityId.description: The ID of an identity from the $(doc:accounts) API. Defaults to the default identity. The permission <permission>accountsRead</permission> is required to include the <val>identityId</val>.

isPlainText.description: Whether the message should be sent as plain text or as HTML. Prefers a specified <value>plainTextBody</value> over a specified <value>body</value>.

newsgroups.description: A single newsgroup name or an array of newsgroup names.

overrideDefaultFccFolder.description: This value overrides the default fcc setting (defined by the used identity) for this message. Either a $(ref:folders.MailFolder) specifying the folder for the copy of the sent message, or an empty string to not save a copy at all.

plainTextBody.description: The content for a plain text message. A specified <value>body</value> will be preferred, except when <value>isPlainText</value> is specified as well.

returnReceipt.description: Add the Disposition-Notification-To header to the message to requests the recipients email client to send a reply once the message has been received. Recipient server may strip the header and the recipient might ignore the request.

description: The messages.tags API allows to manage the user's message tags.

events.description: Fired when a new message tag has been created.
events.name: onCreated

events.description: Fired when one or more properties of a message tag have been updated.
events.name: onUpdated

parameters.description: Unique tag identifier of the updated message tag.
parameters.name: key

parameters.description: The changed message tag properties.
parameters.name: changedProperties

parameters.description: The old values of the changed message tag properties.
parameters.name: oldProperties

events.description: Fired when a message tag has been deleted.
events.name: onDeleted

parameters.description: Unique tag identifier of the deleted message tag.
parameters.name: key

functions.description: Returns a list of tags that can be set on messages, and their human-friendly name, colour, and sort order.
functions.name: list

functions.description: Returns a message tag identified by its key.
functions.name: get

parameters.description: The key of the message tag to retrieve.
parameters.name: key

functions.description: Creates a new message tag and returns the associated key. Tagging a message will store the tag's key in the user's message. Throws if the specified tag key is used already.
functions.name: create

parameters.description: Unique tag identifier (will be converted to lower case). Must not include <var>()<>{/%*"</var> or spaces. Will be auto-generated if not provided.
parameters.name: key

parameters.description: Human-readable tag name.
parameters.name: tag

parameters.description: Tag color in hex format (i.e.: <var>#000080</var> for navy blue).
parameters.name: color

functions.description: Updates a message tag. Throws if the specified tag key does not exist.
functions.name: update

parameters.description: Unique tag identifier (will be converted to lower case). Must not include <var>()<>{/%*"</var> or spaces.
parameters.name: key

functions.description: Deletes a message tag, removing it from the list of known tags. Its key will not be removed from tagged messages, but they will appear untagged. Recreating a deleted tag, will make all former tagged messages appear tagged again.
functions.name: delete

parameters.description: Unique tag identifier (will be converted to lower case). Must not include <var>()<>{/%*"</var> or spaces.
parameters.name: key

color.description: Tag color in upper case hex format (i.e.: <var>#000080</var> for navy blue).
Tag color in upper case hex format (i.e.: <var>#000080</var> for navy blue).

types.description: Used for filtering messages by tag in various methods. Note that functions using this type may have a partial implementation.

mode.description: Whether <var>all</var> of the tag filters must apply, <var>any</var> of them, or <var>none</var>. The <var>none</var> mode ignores the provided filters and selects only messages without any tags.

tags.description: A dictionary object with one or more filter condition as key-value pairs, the key being the tag to filter on, and the value being a boolean expression, requesting whether a message must include (true) or exclude (false) the tag. For a list of available tags, call the $(ref:messages.tags.list) method.
